findings.title: FallbackLocaleList calls SiteSetting before DB may be ready
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale during I18n fallback resolution, which can be invoked very early in boot (e.g. during other initializers, rake tasks, migrations) before the database/connection is available. This risks raising ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError or similar during tasks like db:create, assets:precompile, or any I18n.t call executed prior to DB readiness, unlike the previous config.i18n.fallbacks = true approach which used static fallback rules.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! reads/mutates @loaded_locales without synchronization
findings.body: ensure_loaded! checks and lazily initializes @loaded_locales outside of LOAD_MUTEX before calling load_locale (which itself synchronizes). The initial `@loaded_locales ||= []` is a race: under concurrent requests, two threads could both see @loaded_locales as nil and reassign it, potentially losing already-loaded-locale tracking or causing redundant loads. This should be done inside the mutex or guarded consistently with the rest of the class to avoid the known race in multi-threaded Rails deployments.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! triggers repeated SiteSetting lookups and fallback list per request
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] is called every time set_locale runs (every request) and queries SiteSetting.default_locale each time, building a new array. Since this replaces a previously built-in Rails i18n fallback resolution (config.i18n.fallbacks = true), the cost of SiteSetting lookups on every request could add overhead unless SiteSetting itself is cached; worth confirming caching behavior is adequate.
